text: Paul reminds the Corinthians of the good news he preached, which they accepted and stand on.
It saves them, if they hold to what he told them and did not believe in vain.
He passed on what he himself received as most important: Christ died for our sins, as the Scriptures said.
He was buried and raised on the third day, again as the Scriptures said.
He showed himself to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
After that he appeared to over five hundred believers at once, most still alive, a few now dead.
Then he appeared to James, and then to all the apostles.
Last of all he appeared to Paul too, like someone born at the wrong time.
Paul calls himself the least of the apostles, unfit for the title because he persecuted the church.
Yet by God's grace he is what he is, and that grace was not wasted.
He worked harder than the others, though he credits God's grace; all the apostles preach the same message and the Corinthians believed it.
But if Christ is preached as raised, how can some of you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
If there is no resurrection, then Christ has not been raised either.
And if Christ is not raised, preaching and faith are both empty.
The apostles would then be false witnesses, claiming God raised Christ when he did not.
If the dead are not raised, Christ was not raised.
And if Christ was not raised, their faith is worthless and they remain in their sins.
Those who died believing in Christ would be lost as well.
If hope in Christ covers only this life, believers deserve more pity than anyone.
But in fact Christ has been raised, the first sample of the harvest of those who have died.
Death came by a man, and so does the resurrection of the dead.
As everyone dies through Adam, everyone will be made alive through Christ.
Each in turn: Christ first, then those who belong to him when he comes.
Then comes the end, when he hands the kingdom to the Father after destroying every rival power.
He must reign until all his enemies are under his feet.
Death is the last enemy to be destroyed.
Scripture says everything is put under him, which plainly excludes God who does the putting.
When all is subject to the Son, he too will be subject to God, so that God is all in all.
Otherwise, what of those baptized on behalf of the dead? Why do it if the dead are not raised?
And why would Paul and his friends face danger every hour?
He says he faces death daily, and boasts of the Corinthians as proof; he fought wild opposition at Ephesus.
If there is no resurrection, he says, we may as well eat and drink, since tomorrow we die.
He warns them not to be misled: bad company ruins good character.
Come to your senses and stop sinning; some of you do not know God, and he says this to shame them.
Someone will ask how the dead are raised and with what kind of body.
Paul answers that a seed you sow must die before it comes to life.
What you sow is bare grain, not the plant it will become.
God gives it the body he chooses, each seed its own.
Not all flesh is alike: people, animals, birds and fish each differ.
There are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, each with its own splendor.
The sun, moon and stars shine differently, and star differs from star.
So it is with the resurrection: what is sown perishable is raised imperishable.
Sown in dishonor, raised in glory; sown in weakness, raised in power.
Sown a natural body, raised a spiritual body; if there is one kind there is also the other.
Scripture says the first man Adam became a living being, and the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
The spiritual is not first; the natural comes first, then the spiritual.
The first man was from the earth, made of dust; the second man is from heaven.
Those of the earth are like the man of dust, those of heaven like the man of heaven.
As we have borne the image of the man of dust, we will bear the image of the man of heaven.
Flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom, and the perishable cannot inherit the imperishable.
Paul tells them a mystery: not all will die, but all will be changed.
It will happen in a flash, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet, when the dead are raised imperishable and we are changed.
This perishable body must put on the imperishable, this mortal body immortality.
When that happens, the saying comes true: death is swallowed up in victory.
Death, where is your victory? Death, where is your sting?
Sin is death's sting, and the law gives sin its power.
But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
So, dear friends, stand firm and do not be moved, always giving yourselves to the Lord's work, since your labor in him is never wasted.
